answer: Spectral inlet registration.** Each identity must occupy a distinct narrowband channel in a shared physical inlet (RF or acoustic) and hold it continuously. A ridge detector at the boundary verifies the signal's phase drift matches a registered hardware fingerprint. Every mirror node cross-checks neighbors, so one device cannot broadcast from multiple channels without detectable echo correlation. Attackers pay by acquiring separate certified transceivers and physical siting per identity—the cost scales with hardware and location, not capital, making mass sybils impractical.
